exercise.name: Lever Lying Chest Press (plate loaded)

reference.title: Lever Lying Chest Press (plate loaded)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

equipment: Plate-loaded lying chest press (iso-lateral lever arms over a flat bench)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the handles come down, breathe out as you press up.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, short pause, about 1.3 s press

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Plate load is user-chosen: start with light plates on the horns and press with the back on the pad.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then load; slower return

cues.text: Lie on the bench with the head, upper back and buttocks on the pad and the feet flat; palms down on the handles over the chest, arms extended.
Breathe in and lower the handles along their arc to beside the middle of the chest, elbows about 45-60 degrees from the trunk.
Pause with the hands just above the chest line; shoulder blades squeezed back on the bench.
Breathe out and press up along the arc until the arms are long.
Hold the arms long with the shoulder blades still on the bench.

mistakes.fix: Keep the buttocks on the bench and the feet flat.
Keep the elbows about 45-60 degrees from the trunk.

mistakes.mistake: Shoulders rolling forward at the top
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulder blades on the bench.

kinematics.norm: From well bent with the hands beside the chest to nearly straight (clinical opinion)
About 45-60 degrees from the trunk at the chest (clinical opinion)
Pronated: palms down on horizontal handles (clinical opinion)
The handles ride the lever arc over the chest, from a pivot behind the head (clinical opinion)
Lying on a flat bench: the same body position as the bench press; pectoralis activity was similar across stable and unstable presses at matched loads (Saeterbakken 2011; Calatayud 2015)
Controlled, about 2 s back and 1-1.5 s press (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #5096, Lever Lying Chest Press (plate loaded), video (movement reference)

Saeterbakken, van den Tillaar and Fimland 2011, a comparison of muscle activity and 1-RM strength of three chest-press exercises with different stability requirements (J Sports Sci 29(5):533-538; PubMed 21225489)

Calatayud, Borreani, Colado, Martin, Tella and Andersen 2015, bench press and push-up at comparable levels of muscle activity results in similar strength gains (J Strength Cond Res 29(1):246-253; elastic-band push-ups)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Load is user-chosen: start light and press without the back leaving the pad.
At the end of the set let the handles come back under control before letting go.
Set the start position so the handles are within reach while lying; rack the handles on their stops before sitting up.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: shorten the range so the hands stop in front of the chest.
Low back discomfort: keep both feet flat and the back on the pad.
progressions: Slower return with a pause at the chest.
